title: Why Does Ice Cream Give You BRAIN FREEZE? 🧊
description:
One big slurp of something cold and your forehead freezes. But the cold went in your mouth! The cold hits the roof of your mouth, the blood vessels there squeeze tight and then fling wide open, and blood rushes into an artery at the front of the brain. In one study, the pain lasted exactly as long as that rush. Scientists think it's your body flooding in warm blood to protect your brain... it just overdoes it.

The pain travels up a big nerve in your face (the trigeminal nerve), and your brain blames the wrong spot: your forehead. And yes, gulping makes it worse. A 13-year-old tested it, and the study was published in a real medical journal in 2002. The fix: press your tongue to the roof of your mouth. Or just slow down.
